topic.subject: social
topic.title: The Vedic period
topic.scope: Rigveda, sabha and samiti, varna, megaliths, early Vedic life

misconceptions.statement: Megaliths were houses built for giants to live in.
misconceptions.why: The word 'mega' sounds like 'giant' and students often associate large stone structures with fairy tales or mythical beings.
misconceptions.fix: Megaliths were large stone structures used to mark burial sites for deceased people, not dwellings for living beings.

probe.question: Why did people build such large stone circles?
probe.wrong_answer: They were built as giant houses for people who were much taller than us.

misconceptions.statement: All megaliths contain the same items because everyone was buried the same way.
misconceptions.why: Students often assume historical practices were uniform across all regions and social classes.
misconceptions.fix: Burial goods varied significantly depending on the wealth and status of the deceased, with some graves having more gold or pottery than others.

probe.question: Would you find the same number of pots in every megalithic grave?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because everyone followed the same rule for burying people.

concepts.name: The Rigveda and Early Vedic Life

misconceptions.statement: The Rigveda was written down in a book as soon as it was composed.
misconceptions.why: Students assume that because they read it in a book today, it must have been recorded that way originally.
misconceptions.fix: The hymns were composed and memorized orally for many generations before being written down centuries later.

probe.question: How did people learn the hymns of the Rigveda?
probe.wrong_answer: They read them from the original books kept in the library.

misconceptions.statement: Early Vedic people lived in large, permanent cities like Harappa.
misconceptions.why: Students often conflate different periods of ancient Indian history into one single timeline.
misconceptions.fix: Early Vedic people were largely pastoralists living in smaller settlements or moving with their cattle, unlike the urban Harappan civilization.

probe.question: What kind of houses did people in the Rigvedic period live in?
probe.wrong_answer: They lived in big brick cities with drainage systems.

misconceptions.statement: The Sabha and Samiti were modern-day parliaments with elected members.
misconceptions.why: Students project modern political structures onto ancient assemblies to make sense of them.
misconceptions.fix: These were tribal assemblies where elders or common people met to discuss matters, not elected legislative bodies.

probe.question: Who could vote in the Samiti?
probe.wrong_answer: All the citizens voted for their representatives just like we do today.

misconceptions.statement: The Varna system was always based on birth from the very beginning.
misconceptions.why: Students often assume that social structures they see today have always existed in the same rigid form.
misconceptions.fix: In the early Vedic period, the Varna system was more flexible and based on occupation rather than being strictly hereditary.

probe.question: Could a person change their Varna in the early Vedic period?
probe.wrong_answer: No, you were born into your Varna and could never change it.
